subject: Monthly step-up commits, surge true-up, and launch-season discount structure
messages:
From: Samantha Park <samantha@launchly.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial proposal for Launchly launch ramp

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the proposal — appreciate the clear ramp options. A few quick questions from our side before we take this to procurement:  

- Can you walk me through how the step-up commit works month-to-month? Are we billed on the committed amount or actual usage?
- Is there a quarterly true-up if we exceed a commit in a given month (we have a sizable launch spike window)?
- Any protections for burst/surge during launches so we don’t hit exorbitant overage rates?

We’re targeting a 3-month post-launch growth window where token usage could be 3–4x baseline for 2–4 weeks. Want to avoid a surprise billing event.

If possible, can you send an example schedule that includes a month-by-month commit and the math on discounts/units?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Park
Head of Product, Launchly
[Attachment: usage-forecast-q3.csv (csv)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@launchly.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-13T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Monthly step-up commits, surge true-up, and launch-season discount structure

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up top, details below:  

1) Billing: charged on actual usage, with committed discounts applied as a monthly baseline (you get discounted per-token pricing up to your committed spend for the month).
2) True-up: yes — we offer a monthly true-up model (final bill reconciles committed units vs actual usage). Excess usage is billed at the overage rate, but we can include a capped true-up for launch months per the deal.
3) Surge protections: we can configure automatic fallback pricing and a temporary burst bucket (pre-funded commit) for launch windows to smooth billing spikes.

Attached is a worked example showing a 3-month step-up cadence, the effective per-token price at each tier, and a sample true-up with a 20% capped overage protection for two launch months.

Key ask: if you can share the forecast you attached with the weeks you expect peak traffic, Rafael and I will draft a contract exhibit with explicit burst caps.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_proposal_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-14T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Draft contract language for true-up and surge buckets

Tessa — forwarding suggested legal language for the contract exhibit. I highlighted two options: (A) fixed monthly step-ups with a capped true-up (preferred for predictability), or (B) flexible monthly true-up with higher overage discounts but no cap (better for short-term launch optimization).

Forwarded message:
> From: Legal Ops <legal@redwood.ai>
> To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
> Date: 2027-04-13T16:30:00-07:00
> Subject: Suggested exhibit wording (true-up / burst)
>
> Option A (capped true-up):
> "Customer will commit to a monthly baseline (as defined in Exhibit A). For any month in which actual usage exceeds the monthly baseline, Customer will be invoiced for excess usage at the overage rate, subject to a capped true-up equal to 20% of the monthly baseline for no more than two months per 12-month period. Temporary burst capacity beyond the capped true-up will be billed from the Customer's pre-funded burst bucket at the committed burst rate."
>
> Option B (flexible true-up):
> "Customer will be invoiced monthly for actual usage. Committed baseline discounts apply to the first N tokens as defined in Exhibit A. Excess usage will be billed at the overage rate; Redwood will apply a 10% discount to the overage rate during the first two launch months of the customer-defined launch window."
>
> Notes: include an explicit process for Customer to notify Redwood of planned launch windows at least 7 business days in advance to enable burst bucket provisioning.

Rafael

From: Samantha Park <samantha@launchly.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Monthly step-up commits, surge true-up, and launch-season discount structure

Thanks both — this is helpful. Launchly prefers predictability, so Option A (capped true-up + pre-funded burst bucket) is the direction we want, with the following adjustments:  

- Cap should be 25% for up to two months (higher safety margin given our traffic model).
- Bursts: we want the ability to draw an additional limited emergency buffer (one-off) if integration issues cause an unexpected surge; propose emergency buffer billed at the standard overage rate but excluded from the cap once used.
- Reporting: weekly token usage dashboard for the launch window and an automatic alert when we reach 75% of the monthly baseline.

Can you confirm you can commit to the dashboard and the 7 business day launch notice requirement? Also attaching our redlines to the contract.

Best,
Samantha
[Attachment: contract_redlines.docx (docx)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@launchly.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Monthly step-up commits, surge true-up, and launch-season discount structure

Samantha — all points workable. Summary of agreed changes to include in the final exhibit:  

- Commitment cadence: 3-month step-up (Month 1 = 250k tokens, Month 2 = 500k tokens, Month 3 = 750k tokens) with monthly reconciliation against actuals.
- Capped true-up: 25% of the monthly baseline, applicable for up to two launch months per 12-month period.
- Burst bucket: pre-funded burst bucket available for each launch month; emergency buffer (one-off) allowed and billed at standard overage; emergency buffer is excluded from the capped-true-up protection once drawn.
- Alerts & reporting: weekly dashboard during launch window and automated 75% baseline threshold alerts — Aditya will own provisioning.
- Notice: Launchly will provide 7 business days notice to enable burst provisioning.

Next steps: Rafael will incorporate language into contract exhibit and send for your legal review. Aditya will provision the dashboard and the burst bucket templates and share a runbook. Once legal signs off, we’ll issue a DocuSign for the exhibit amendment and the first month’s pre-funded burst purchase.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth launch.

Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
